cases.sentence: Отвечает ли мудрый знанием взятым с ___?
cases.explain: The preposition с (with/from) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Твой грех побуждает твои ___, ты усвоил язык нечестивых.
cases.explain: The transitive verb побуждает (teaches/urges) takes the direct object in the accusative case.

cases.sentence: С нами седовласы и старики, старше, чем твой ___.
cases.explain: The comparative construction requires the genitive case for the person being compared.
The transitive verb подслушал (heard) takes the direct object in the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Кто такой человек, чтобы ему быть чистым, и рожденный ___, чтобы быть праведным?
cases.explain: The preposition рожденный requires the instrumental case to indicate the means or agent.

cases.sentence: Им одним была отдана ___, и чужой среди них не ходил.
cases.explain: Земля is the subject that was given, standing in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: На что он не обманывается, полагаясь на ___?
cases.explain: The transitive verb полагаясь (relying) takes the direct object in the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Бесплодным будет безбожных ___, и огонь истребит шатры вымогателей.
cases.explain: Сборище is the subject of the verb будет, requiring the nominative case.

reading.ru: «Отвечает ли мудрый знанием взятым с ветра?
reading.question: What does Eliphaz ask about the wise man?
options: Does he answer with vain knowledge from the wind?
reading.correct: Does he answer with vain knowledge from the wind?
reading.explain: Eliphaz asks Отвечает ли мудрый знанием взятым с ветра — 'Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge from the wind?'

reading.ru: А ты и страх перед Богом потерял, и молитву к Богу считаешь малостью?
reading.question: What accusations does Eliphaz make against Job?
options: Job has lost the fear of God and considers prayer worthless
reading.correct: Job has lost the fear of God and considers prayer worthless
reading.explain: Eliphaz says А ты и страх перед Богом потерял, и молитву к Богу считаешь малостью — 'You have lost the fear of God and consider prayer worthless.'

reading.ru: Твой грех побуждает твои уста, ты усвоил язык нечестивых.
reading.question: What does Eliphaz say sin has caused Job to do?
options: His sin teaches his mouth and he has adopted the language of the wicked
His sin leads him to repentance
reading.correct: His sin teaches his mouth and he has adopted the language of the wicked
reading.explain: Eliphaz declares Твой грех побуждает твои уста, ты усвоил язык нечестивых — 'Your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.'

reading.ru: Что знаешь ты, чего бы мы не знали? Что понимаешь, чего бы мы не поняли?
reading.question: What is Eliphaz implying about Job's knowledge?
options: Job knows nothing that they do not already know
Job is the wisest among them
Job understands God better than they do
Job has unique insight from God
reading.correct: Job knows nothing that they do not already know
reading.explain: Eliphaz asks rhetorical questions implying that Job has no knowledge or understanding that they lack.

reading.ru: С нами седовласы и старики, старше, чем твой отец.
reading.question: What claim does Eliphaz make about his companions?
options: They are gray-haired and very aged, older than Job's father
They are from a distant land
reading.correct: They are gray-haired and very aged, older than Job's father
reading.explain: Eliphaz says С нами седовласы и старики, старше, чем твой отец — 'With us are the gray-headed and very aged men, much elder than your father.'

reading.ru: Все дни свои мучается нечестивый, отчитаны все годы притеснителя.
reading.question: How does Eliphaz describe the life of the wicked?
options: The wicked man writhes in pain all his days, the years of the oppressor are numbered
The wicked prosper and are blessed
The wicked live in peace and comfort
The wicked are honored and respected
reading.correct: The wicked man writhes in pain all his days, the years of the oppressor are numbered
reading.explain: The text says Все дни свои мучается нечестивый, отчитаны все годы притеснителя — 'The wicked man writhes in pain all his days, even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.'
